title: Unique identifier shared at source
description: Device ID is explicitly transferred as a unique identifier that can be used to link data across sessions and identify the user.
assumptions: Device ID is a unique identifier for the wearable device and its user.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in transit
description: GPS traces, timestamps, and exercise sessions can be combined to identify individuals through quasi-identifier analysis.
assumptions: Multiple data attributes are available for linkage analysis.

title: Unique identifier in shared data
description: Device ID serves as a unique reference to the identity of the data subject.
assumptions: Device ID is unique to the user's device.

title: Revealing attributes in metadata
description: GPS traces and timestamps in the data flow reveal location and activity patterns that can support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Location and activity data can be used to identify individuals.

title: Sensitive data type collected
description: GPS traces and timestamps are sensitive personal data types that may be collected beyond functional requirements.
assumptions: Exercise sessions and GPS data are functionally required for the app's purpose.

title: Profiling of individual through exercise patterns
description: Exercise session data can be analyzed for patterns to link data to the individual and profile their fitness habits.
assumptions: Exercise data is analyzed for patterns that can identify the user.

title: Unnecessary data treatment and analysis
description: Data may be further treated, analyzed, and enriched in ways not necessary to achieve the functionality of the system.
assumptions: Additional analysis beyond basic exercise tracking may be performed.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Users may not be aware that their sensor data is being collected, processed, and shared with the companion app.
assumptions: Users may not fully understand the data processing activities.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (GPS traces, timestamps, device ID) may be processed than is actually needed for the functional goals of the system.
assumptions: Data minimization principle requires only functionally necessary data to be processed.

title: Linking through GPS location data
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can serve as quasi-identifiers that can be combined with other data to link individuals to specific times and places.
assumptions: Assumes location data is collected and stored in a way that preserves temporal and spatial precision.

title: Location data contains quasi-identifiers
description: GPS coordinates combined with timestamps can uniquely identify individuals and their movements, serving as quasi-identifiers.
assumptions: Assumes location data is precise enough to distinguish between different individuals.

title: Highly sensitive data type collected
description: GPS location data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required for the app's functionality.
assumptions: Assumes the app's primary function may not require continuous GPS tracking.

title: Fine-grained location data disclosed
description: GPS location data is of very fine-grained granularity, potentially disclosing more precise location information than functionally needed.
assumptions: Assumes the app may not need such precise location data for its core functionality.

title: Unawareness of location tracking
description: Users may not be fully aware that their GPS location is being continuously tracked and stored in the location history store.
assumptions: Assumes users may not have clear visibility into the extent of location data collection.

title: Lack of control over data retention
description: Users may lack control over how long their location history is stored and whether it can be deleted or rectified.
assumptions: Assumes the app may not provide clear mechanisms for users to manage their location data retention.

title: Excessive data retention
description: Location history may be stored longer than functionally needed for the app's purpose, increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Assumes the app may not have clear retention policies for location data.

title: Data accessible to more parties than needed
description: Location history stored in DS2 may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 may be accessible to internal services or third parties beyond what is needed.

title: Linking through metadata in data flow
description: The data flow itself may contain metadata (e.g., timestamps, device identifiers) that can be used to link individuals across different data sources.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow may include additional identifying metadata beyond the location data itself.

title: Quasi-identifier combining data of a single individual
description: Calorie, weight, and exercise logs combined may serve as quasi-identifiers that can link data to individuals when shared with analytics service.
assumptions: Assumes logs are shared without additional anonymization

title: Profiling an individual
description: Health Analytics Service performs health-condition analysis which may involve profiling individuals based on their health log patterns.
assumptions: Analytics service analyzes patterns across multiple data points

title: Revealing attributes
description: Health logs contain revealing attributes (calorie, weight, exercise) that support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Health logs contain identifiable health information

title: Treatment, analysis, enrichment
description: Health-condition analysis may involve unnecessary treatment or enrichment of health data beyond functional requirements.
assumptions: Analytics service may perform additional analysis beyond health-condition analysis

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Health logs may contain more personal data than actually needed for health-condition analysis functionality.
assumptions: All health log data is collected and processed

title: Unique identifier in data flow
description: Data flow may contain unique identifiers embedded in health logs that enable linking across sessions.
assumptions: Health logs contain unique identifiers

title: System responses
description: System responses from analytics service may reveal existence of health data or processing activities.
assumptions: Analytics service provides responses to queries

title: Profiling an individual through location history analysis
description: Location history data is analyzed to derive daily routine and movement patterns, which constitutes profiling an individual based on their location-based behavior patterns.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combining data of a single individual
description: Location history data combined with session identifiers and timestamps can serve as quasi-identifiers that link location data to specific individuals.

title: Profiling a group of individuals through movement patterns
description: Movement patterns derived from location history can reveal insights about larger groups of individuals, potentially transferring knowledge about group behaviors to other individuals through known relations.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location history data contains revealing attributes that support the identification of data subjects, including revealing patterns about daily routines and movement habits.

title: Sensitive data type sensitivity
description: Location history is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for the functional purpose of deriving movement patterns.

title: Excessive volume of location data processed
description: The volume of location history data processed may exceed what is functionally needed to derive daily routine and movement patterns.

title: Unnecessary treatment and analysis of location data
description: Location history data is further analyzed and enriched to derive movement patterns, which may be more extensive than functionally needed for the system's purpose.

title: Personal data made accessible to predetermined set of parties
description: Location history data is made accessible to the Health Analytics Service, which is a predetermined set of parties that may not be functionally necessary for all use cases.

title: Unawareness of processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being queried and analyzed to derive daily routine and movement patterns.

title: Lack of data subject control over processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control over how their location history is processed, including preferences for what patterns are derived and how long data is retained.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (location history) is processed than is actually needed for the functional purpose of deriving daily routine and movement patterns.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for data subject rights regarding location history processing (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking.

title: Profiling an individual through inferred health insights
description: The Health Analytics Service shares inferred health insights (risk indicators, summaries, trend flags) that were derived from profiling individual health data, enabling linkage of this data to the individual.
assumptions: The inferred insights are derived from individual health data through profiling/derivation processes.

title: Linking through group insights
description: The data flow transmits insights about health conditions that could be used to link individuals to groups or transfer knowledge about group membership patterns.
assumptions: The trend flags and routine summaries may contain group-level patterns that can be used for linking.

title: Revealing attributes in health insights
description: The Companion Mobile App receives health-condition risk indicators and routine summaries that contain revealing attributes which support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: The health insights contain attributes that can be used to identify or re-identify the individual.

title: Identified information in data flow
description: The data flow itself contains identified information (health insights) that can be used to identify the data subject.
assumptions: The inferred insights contain unique or quasi-identifiers that can identify the individual.

title: Data type granularity exceeds functional need
description: The data flow transmits health insights at a fine-grained level that may be more granular than functionally needed for the Companion Mobile App's intended use.
assumptions: The Companion Mobile App may not need all the detailed health insights being transmitted.

title: Data exposed to predetermined set of parties
description: The data flow exposes health insights to a predetermined set of parties (the Companion Mobile App) that may be more parties than functionally necessary.
assumptions: The Companion Mobile App may not be the only party that should receive this health data.

title: Data propagation to other services
description: The Companion Mobile App may propagate the received health insights to other services where they are not needed.
assumptions: The Companion Mobile App may share the health insights with third parties.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The Companion Mobile App may process more personal data than is actually needed for its intended functionality.
assumptions: The Companion Mobile App may not need all the health insights being received.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in health data
description: Health and location dataset may contain unique identifiers that can be used to link data to specific individuals across systems
assumptions: Health data typically includes personal identifiers

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of health and location data can serve as quasi-identifiers that enable linking to individuals
assumptions: Health and location data together can uniquely identify individuals

title: Processing of unique identifiers
description: Health and location dataset contains unique references to identity of data subjects
assumptions: Health data includes personal identifiers

title: Excessive volume of personal data
description: Full health and location dataset may contain more personal data than functionally needed for analytics purposes
assumptions: Not all health data is necessary for the analytics service

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing full health and location dataset may violate GDPR data minimization principle by collecting more data than actually needed
assumptions: GDPR applies to this processing activity

title: Identified information in metadata
description: Data flow metadata may contain identifying information about the parties involved in the data transfer
assumptions: Network metadata can reveal communication patterns and parties

title: Data accessible to predetermined external party
description: Cloud hosting provider is a predetermined external party with access to health and location data
assumptions: Cloud provider has access to all data received

title: Unawareness of data subject about hosting
description: Data subjects may not be aware their health and location data is being hosted at third-party cloud provider
assumptions: Data subjects are not informed about cloud hosting arrangement

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Data replication at cloud provider may store data longer than functionally needed
assumptions: Replication extends data retention beyond original processing needs
